headline: Choose each later index to enumerate every subset once
statement: Return all subsets of an array of distinct integers, including the empty subset. The order of subsets and the order of values within a subset do not matter.
intuition: A subset can be represented uniquely by an increasing sequence of input indices. At each call, the current path already represents one subset; choosing any later index extends it into a larger one.
approach: Start with an empty path at index zero.
Record a copy of the path at the beginning of every call.
For every index at or after start, append its value, recurse from i+1, then remove it.
correctness: The empty path represents the empty subset. Every nonempty subset has one unique increasing index sequence; the recursion follows that sequence and records it exactly once. Increasing start prevents an index from being selected twice or the same subset from being generated in another order.
bruteForce: Iterate all bit masks from 0 to 2^n-1 and include values whose bits are set. This is also optimal in output order of growth.

complexity.explanation: There are 2^n subsets and copying their contents totals n×2^(n-1) entries.

pitfalls: Copy path rather than storing a shared mutable list.
Recurse from i+1 to prevent repeated indices.
